analysis.title: GS MORNING: 1) FX Trader Call Takeaways, 2) Trading Energy Relief, 3) 2027 Capex Outlook, 4) The Upside to Inflation and 5) Equities Update
key_insights: US economics: October CPI printed +30bps m/m even though noisy categories (airfares, health insurance, car prices) came in lower. GS says this makes the transitory-inflation view harder to hold and expects near-term inflation forecasts to move somewhat higher, a move toward hotter, not a sea change.

EM FX trading likes long CNH, funded with a basket of EUR and SGD, on a stronger USD backdrop. October trade surplus above $100bn has driven RMB appreciation. The 2% hike in the foreign currency deposit RRR and the one-off higher onshore fixing were symbolic moves meant to slow appreciation, not reverse it.
GS would re-enter long CNH once the spot-fixing gap is near -200/-300 pips, absent material external shocks. It expects faster-than-carry appreciation into January on seasonal exporter repatriation.

FX strategy (Jenkins): energy prices have fallen significantly month-to-date and GS's Energy FX factor is down about 2.2% in November. FX reacts more to oil-higher days than oil-lower days, and that asymmetry has played out over the past two weeks.

Brent is just under midway through its energy shock range, while TTF is closer to its highs. NOKSEK has held more of its gains, consistent with stickier energy passthrough to that cross. AUDNZD is further off its highs, with domestic factors playing a larger role.

US capex: real business fixed investment grew at an 11% annualized rate in 2026Q1-Q3, with another strong quarter expected in Q4. AI spending, much of it on imported capital goods, accounted for over half of that growth.
GS estimates AI-related hardware and IP spending will exceed $900bn annualized by end-2026 (up $550bn from 2025) and reach $1.4tn by end-2027 (up a further $500bn), about 4% of US GDP.
AI investment is estimated to add 5.3pp to true 2027 capex growth but 4.3pp to measured capex growth, and 0.6pp to true GDP growth but 0.2pp to measured GDP growth.
GS forecasts 2027 real business fixed investment growth of 8% Q4/Q4 versus consensus 4.2%, and 2027 real GDP growth of 2.4% Q4/Q4.

Midterm risk to AI investment is modest for now. GS expects newly elected Democratic governors in Texas, Georgia and Michigan, which hold over a third of planned US data centre capacity, to impose moratoria on new data centres. These should hit only unpermitted projects, leaving most 2027 construction unaffected. Stricter or longer moratoria are a downside risk mainly in 2028-2029.

Global economics (Peters): core inflation has mostly surprised to the downside in major economies since the start of the war in Iran, but US September and October inflation surprised to the upside. Global import and producer prices have risen and broadened.

Upstream price increases typically take 6-12 months to pass through to consumer prices, so residual pressure should continue into 1H 2027. Country team forecasts have been revised up through June 2027 versus February 2026.

Consensus has historically under-weighted upstream price changes. The historical shock-to-surprise relationship implies 0.1-0.2pp cumulative upside to consensus inflation over the next 9 months, which could prompt modest further central bank tightening in early 2027.

Equities flow desk (Privorotsky): the rally was narrow. Semis led (SOX +5.5%, ARM +12%, MU +12%) while MSFT, META and AMZN closed lower. Nvidia governance issues are forcing a significant rebalancing of capital, and NVDA fell roughly 9% overnight, weighing on Asia tech.
Retail Favorites basket (GSXURFAV) rose 495bps, its third best day in three years. Three sub-$4 stocks accounted for 32% of US tape volume.

Vol and positioning: the SPX vol curve un-inverted, dealer skew flattened, and systematic L/S managers posted their best two-day return in nearly three years (+2.15%). Breadth remains narrow. The open question is whether the bid is mechanical short covering on low positioning or the start of something durable.

AI infrastructure: GS separates fundamental compute demand from valuation multiples. Hyperscalers are best positioned given balance sheets and contracted infrastructure. Four overhangs: higher cost of capital, power/permitting constraints, supply/demand balance entering 2028, and monetization velocity relative to capex. GS expects episodic, high-beta rallies rather than buy and hold.

Risk view: this may be only a bear market rally. A durable breakout likely needs lower rates, lower energy and broader leadership (hyperscalers, transportation, cyclicals, aerospace, with defense washed out). An aggressive hiking cycle and high oil work against those groups. Base case is chop rather than breakout, with low positioning and high vol as short-term tailwinds.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning has been reset materially, vol remains elevated, and the market has absorbed an extraordinary amount of bad news. Low positioning and high vol are powerful short-term tailwinds, and the market absorbed heavy Nvidia pressure without broader capitulation.
tension_points.bear_case: The rally may be just a bear market rally and short covering, with narrow breadth. An aggressive hiking cycle and stubbornly high oil prices make it hard for cyclicals, transports and defense to lead sustainably.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A durable breakout would need lower rates, lower energy and broader leadership. Without them GS expects the market to chop rather than break out.

tension_points.bull_case: GS forecasts 2027 real business fixed investment growth of 8% Q4/Q4, far above the 4.2% consensus, with AI the dominant driver of investment growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Much AI spending is on imported capital goods, so measured GDP gains (0.2pp) are well below true gains (0.6pp). Stricter data centre moratoria are a risk in 2028-2029.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Stricter or longer-lasting state moratoria on new data centres, particularly affecting 2028-2029 projects.
